text: We're launching Chrono — a wearable that reads your circadian rhythm and adjusts ambient light, audio cues, and notification timing to keep you in flow. The launch film needs to feel calm but inevitable, like watching a sunrise. Target audience: design-literate knowledge workers aged 28–42 who already use Oura or Whoop. The 90-second piece should land in 21 beats: a slow hook on stillness, the reveal of the device on the wrist (~scene 7), three proof scenes showing the app, a customer line, and a closing CTA to pre-order at chrono.co. Brand voice is 'quiet, technical, generous.' Avoid hard-sell language, avoid drone shots, avoid blue tints (we own a warm Nordic palette: bone, oat, deep teal, brass accent). The film will run as the hero asset on chrono.co and as a 60-second cutdown on YouTube pre-roll. Constraints: no licensed music (we have a custom Nils Frahm-style score), no actor voiceover (the device itself 'speaks' via on-screen captions), must include legal mark in scene 21.
